summary: A long 13-turn tau2Airline service session for customer Maya Chen spanning cancellations, a flight change, a cabin upgrade, two new bookings, and a price search. T1 and T3 run clean eligibility checks and correctly refuse to cancel C4C633 and EC4C1C (not within 24h, not Business, no insurance, airline didn't cancel); T3 also denies a compensation request on the Vegas booking because the insurance on the separate round-trip does not transfer. T2 pulls the full reservation list and recalls A2CBB0 (LAX→SFO). T4–T6 change A2CBB0's flight (+$129), T7–T10 book two new itineraries with explicit price math and confirmation, and T11 executes the JFK→MIA booking and a cabin upgrade of A2CBB0 from Economy to Business (+$200, total $329). The two probe turns diverge: T3 is RECALL+APPLY (compensation correctly denied), but T2 is RECALL+MISAPPLY — A2CBB0 is recalled correctly yet the cabin-change-not-allowed policy is never applied, and the T11 upgrade proceeds instead of being refused.

findings.title: Eligibility checks are consistently crisp
findings.body: T1 and T3 both render the four cancellation conditions as an explicit met/not-met table and close with a Deciding › Decline ("None of the four qualifying conditions are met") — the refusal machinery is reliable when the policy is a checklist the agent reads off.

findings.title: The one policy that is a rule, not a checklist, slips
findings.body: The cabin-change restriction has no tidy table, and it is exactly the one the agent misapplies: T2 recalls A2CBB0 but no Evaluate/Deciding tag guards the cabin field, and T11 quietly upgrades Economy→Business — the RECALL+MISAPPLY is a policy that never surfaces as a check.

findings.title: Confirmation discipline is strong but orthogonal to policy
findings.body: Nearly every booking turn (T5, T8, T10) ends in a Grounding › Ask-for-clarification confirmation gate with full price math, yet that discipline governs money and consent, not the cabin-change legality — showing procedural care and policy correctness are separate axes.
